blocks.text: The Math of Workstation Bins: Why 1,000-Count Cases Drive Office Consumable Costs

In a typical 10,000- to 25,000-square-foot commercial office suite, central breakrooms and restrooms contain only six to ten large barrels, whereas open-plan cubicles, private executive offices, and conference rooms house 60 to 150 individual deskside wastebaskets. If a facility manager allows an office administrator to purchase retail 50-count or 100-count drawstring kitchen bags for workstation bins, the per-liner cost explodes by 300% to 500%, and the oversized bags hang clumsily down the sides of 13- to 28-quart bins.

Even when buying commercial grade supplies, deskside liner volume scales rapidly with service frequency. Under US commercial cleaning benchmarks (4.33 weeks per month), a 5x/week daily cleaning schedule equals 21.65 visits per month (260 visits per year), while a 3x/week schedule equals 13.0 visits per month (156 visits per year). In an office with 100 desks cleaned 5x/week, changing every deskside liner every night consumes 2,165 liners per month—over 25,980 liners (26 full 1,000-count cases) per year. Mastering 1,000-count coreless roll specifications and nightly pulling workflows is the single fastest way to optimize both your consumables allowance ($0.012 to $0.025 per sq ft per visit) and your nightly custodial labor efficiency.

blocks.title: ISSA Time Savings of Coreless 'In-Bin' Roll Dispensing
blocks.text: Under ISSA 3,500 sq ft/hour commercial office cleaning production standards (billed at $35 to $65 per labor hour), walking back to a utility cart or wrestling with loose flat-packed bags adds 8 to 12 seconds per workstation. Dropping a 50-count perforated coreless roll of 24x33-inch 8-micron HDPE liners into the bottom of each deskside bin lets the custodian pull a soiled liner while the fresh replacement bag automatically feeds up from underneath—saving 15 to 22 minutes of labor every night across a 100-desk floor.
Why 24x33 Inches and 8-Micron HDPE Is the Universal Office Deskside Standard

Commercial office deskside wastebaskets fall into two standardized molded plastic sizes: the compact 13.6-quart (3.4-gallon) bin measuring roughly 11.4 x 8.25 inches at the rim by 12 inches tall, and the standard 28.1-quart (7-gallon) office wastebasket measuring 14.4 x 10.25 inches at the rim (a 49.3-inch total rim perimeter) by 15 inches tall. A smaller 20x22-inch liner (40-inch perimeter) fits tiny 3-gallon bathroom bins, but it cannot stretch around the 49.3-inch perimeter of a 28-quart rectangular office wastebasket without tearing.

Conversely, a 24x33-inch liner features a 48-inch flat perimeter that stretches smoothly over a 28-quart rectangular rim—or folds neatly around a 13-quart rim—while its 33-inch length easily covers the 15-inch vertical wall plus 5 inches of bottom depth with a secure 8- to 10-inch cuff overhang. Selecting an 8-micron High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) film provides a crisp, leak-proof vapor barrier that holds 10 to 15 pounds of crumpled bond paper, used facial tissues, and damp coffee filters without paying for excess resin thickness.

blocks.text: Implementing the 'Selective Pull & Friday Reline' Protocol in Your Cleaning Contract

Whether you pay a janitorial contractor $0.012 to $0.025 per sq ft per visit for turnkey consumables or buy your own 1,000-count cases on Amazon Business, your written Scope of Work (SOW) determines how fast your crew burns through cases. Most generic janitorial checklists state: 'Empty all wastebaskets and replace liners nightly.' Taken literally, that language forces cleaners to throw away hundreds of pristine plastic liners every week that held nothing more than three dry sheets of printer paper.

items.name: Stage One 50-Bag Coreless Roll Inside Every Workstation Bin
items.text: During initial contract onboarding, have the cleaning crew place a coreless roll of 24x33-inch 8-micron liners directly in the bottom well of each deskside wastebasket and pull the first bag up over the rim.

items.name: Dump Dry Paper Loose Into the 44-Gallon Collector Cart Monday Through Thursday
items.text: When the nightly technician services a workstation, they inspect the deskside bin. If it contains only dry paper or dry wrappers with zero food residue, liquid, or used facial tissues, they tip the bin contents into their mobile 44-gallon collector barrel and leave the clean 24x33 liner in place.

items.name: Pull Soiled Liners Immediately and Complete a Full Floor Reline Every Friday
items.text: Whenever a workstation bin contains used Kleenex tissues, food wrappers, tea bags, or beverage cups, the technician pulls the bag immediately, tearing it off the bottom coreless roll as they lift and cuffing the next bag over the rim. On Friday night (or the final weekly service visit), crews reline any bins showing dust buildup.

blocks.title: Centralized 'Mini-Bin' Policies for High-Density Open Offices
blocks.text: In tech, call-center, and coworking floors exceeding 125 employees per 15,000 sq ft, some facility managers replace under-desk 28-quart trash cans with tiny 3-quart clip-on desk caddies for food wrappers and a full-size 28-quart blue deskside paper bin. Even under traditional 28-quart deskside layouts, switching from 100% nightly bag replacement to selective relining cuts annual 1,000-count case orders from 21 cases down to just 6 cases per 80 workstations.

faqs.q: Will a 24x33-inch trash liner fit a standard 7-gallon (28-quart) rectangular office wastebasket?
faqs.a: Yes. A standard 28-quart commercial rectangular deskside wastebasket measures approximately 14.4 inches long by 10.25 inches wide at the top lip (49.3 inches in perimeter) and 15 inches tall. A 24x33-inch high-density liner has a 48-inch flat perimeter that stretches snugly over the 49.3-inch rim without slipping down inside the bin, while the 33-inch length provides a clean 6- to 8-inch overhang.

faqs.q: What does 'coreless roll' mean on a 1,000-count commercial liner case?
faqs.a: Traditional consumer roll bags are wound around a hollow cardboard cylinder tube, which adds shipping weight, takes up extra storage space, and creates 20 discarded cardboard cores per 1,000-count case. Coreless rolls wind the 50 perforated liners tightly around themselves with no cardboard center tube. This compact diameter lets janitors drop an entire 50-bag roll flat into the bottom of a deskside wastebasket or thread it onto a janitor cart spindle.

faqs.q: When should an office upgrade from 6-micron to 8-micron or 10-micron deskside liners?
faqs.a: If your company enforces a strict 'no eating at desks' policy so workstation bins collect only dry printer paper and sticky notes, a 6-micron HDPE liner is sufficient. However, in modern offices where employees eat lunch at their desks and toss yogurt cups, damp napkins, and used facial tissues into workstation bins, upgrading to an 8-micron HDPE liner (like the Boardwalk 24x33 1,000-count case) provides 33% more film density to prevent liquid pinpoint leaks onto office carpet.

faqs.q: How does workstation density affect our per-square-foot janitorial cleaning rate?
faqs.a: Standard US commercial cleaning rates ($0.09 to $0.15/sq ft for 2,500–9,999 sq ft offices and $0.07 to $0.12/sq ft for 10,000–24,999 sq ft offices) assume a baseline occupant density of one workstation per 150 to 200 square feet, allowing cleaners to hit the 3,500 sq ft/hour ISSA benchmark. If a dense bench-seating layout packs one workstation into every 75 to 90 square feet, the custodian has twice as many deskside bins to empty and wipe per thousand square feet, which can move your quote toward the upper half of the square-footage bracket unless you use selective relining.
